privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Variater is a tool for modelling leveraged buyouts. This page says what it keeps about you, who handles it for us, and how to have it removed.
privacy.storedSignIn: Sign-in is run by Clerk. Clerk holds your email address and, if you sign in with Google, the name and picture Google shares. Variater's own database keeps only Clerk's id for you, never your name or email address.
privacy.storedProfile: The four answers you give when you sign up: country, preferred currency, number format and time zone.
privacy.storedDeals: The deals you save, their earlier versions, the actual results you enter for them, and your settings. With each deal and version we keep which version of the model it was saved with and the IRR and MOIC it gave then, so reopening it can tell you if its results have changed. Nothing from a deal is ever written to a log or an error report.
privacy.storedActivity: A history of what you did and when: a deal created, edited (which fields, never the figures), renamed, archived, a version kept or restored, actual results saved, a download, a deal deleted, changes to your settings, letting a deal count in model validation or stopping it, and, for an administrator, showing or hiding the reference library and proposing, approving or rejecting a reference transaction (public filing data; the library keeps which account reviewed it). It holds no figures, deal names or version labels, so it outlives a deleted deal without keeping anything from it.
privacy.validation: Off unless you switch it on for a deal (Backtest, Plan and actuals). Then, each night, that deal's plan and actual results are run through the model on our server to see whether its outcome fell inside the ranges it predicted. Only counts and rates per region, sector, size and era are kept in the report everyone signed in can see: never the deal, its name, its figures or your account, and a group with fewer than five users' deals shows neither its figures nor how many it holds. Switch it off and the next report leaves the deal out; deleting the deal does the same.
privacy.google: Google shares your name, email address and profile picture with Clerk, only so that you can sign in. Variater asks for nothing else from your Google account and never reads your Google data.
privacy.companies: A company search, and loading a company's figures, sends what you typed (a name, ticker, LEI, ISIN or company number) from our server to the public registers searched: the US SEC (EDGAR), filings.xbrl.org, GLEIF, UK Companies House and Japan's EDINET. They see our server asking, never who you are. The figures are public filings, kept in a store every account shares, with nothing about who asked for them.
privacy.processors: Clerk (sign-in), Vercel (the website), Render (the model API), Neon (the database, in the United States), Supabase (encrypted nightly backups), Upstash (usage counters, keyed by a one-way hash of your id), Sentry (error reports, with deal contents removed) and Better Stack (uptime checks).
privacy.not: No advertising, no selling or sharing of your data, and no tracking cookies: the only cookies are the ones that keep you signed in.
privacy.keep: Your deals, their actual results and your settings stay until you delete them or ask us to delete your account. A deleted deal's activity stays in your account's history until you ask us to delete your account; edits older than a week are merged into one line a day. Encrypted backups are rotated and the oldest is at most a year old.
privacy.contact: To have your account and everything in it deleted, or to ask anything about this policy, open an issue at {link}.

warnings.implied_rating_lowest: Year-one interest cover of {coverage} (EBIT over interest) falls in the {rating} band (below {band_high}), the weakest there is. Companies rated {study_row} defaulted {default_pct} of the time within {years, plural, one {# year} other {# years}}, on average.

The model fills the gap with cash nobody provides; a revolver that can be redrawn, or a later maturity, would fund it.

library.collection_examples: {count, plural, one {# example deal} other {# example deals}}
library.empty_reference_deals: No reference transaction is approved yet. Each joins when two administrators approve it on Review, every figure with its filing.
library.referencesRail: Each transaction joins the library when two administrators other than its proposer approve it. Every figure links to the filing it was read from.
library.awaitingReview: {count, plural, one {# transaction awaits review} other {# transactions await review}}
library.noReferences: None has been approved yet. Each joins the library when two administrators approve it on Review.
library.referencesNotice: {count, plural, one {# transaction} other {# transactions}}, every figure with its filing, where in it and its words. Money is in millions of each deal's currency.
library.sumOfParts: {count, plural, one {The piece below} other {The sum of the # pieces below}}
library.reviewRail: A proposal joins the library on the second approval by an administrator other than its proposer; one rejection decides it. Any finding of the inclusion rules blocks approval; the balance notes are advice.
library.reviewAdminsOnly: Only administrators review reference transactions. The approved ones are on Reference deals.
library.reviewNoDatabase: Reviewing needs a database, and this server has none.
library.reviewBlocked: The inclusion rules refuse it as it stands: see its findings.
library.reviewRefused_403: Not allowed: only an administrator other than the proposer may decide it.
library.reviewRefused_409: Already decided, already reviewed by you, or already proposed.
library.reviewRefused_422: The file is not a reference transaction in the repository's format.
library.balanceNeutral: Leaves the library's balance as it is.
library.replacesApproved: Approving it replaces the version now in the library.
library.cannotOwn: You proposed it: two other administrators decide it.
library.alreadyReviewed: You have reviewed it; it waits for another administrator.
library.cannotBlocked: It can't be approved until the findings are corrected and it is proposed again.
library.proposeRail: Propose a transaction from a file in the format of the repository's library/reference_deals.json: every figure with its filing.
library.proposed: Proposed: two other administrators decide it.
library.problem_unknown_figure: Not a figure the library keeps: {at}.
library.problem_not_a_filing: Not a filing on a regulator's, register's or exchange's site: {at}.
library.problem_debt_exceeds_value: The debt is more than the value paid.
library.problem_closed_in_future: The closing date is in the future.
library.problem_outcome_before_close: The outcome comes before the closing.
library.problem_event_doesnt_match_outcome: The event doesn't fit the outcome.

modelValidation.sampleNote_out_of_time: Outcomes that became known after everything the prediction was made from. Only these test the model.
modelValidation.sampleNote_in_sample: Outcomes the prediction's data already covered, or plans saved after their actuals. Shown for reference, never as the result.
modelValidation.about: Each night the model's default risk is checked against the approved reference transactions, and its IRR ranges and probability of loss against users' deals that opted in and have exited.
modelValidation.anonymity: Users' deals appear only as counts and rates per group. A group holding fewer than five of them shows neither.
modelValidation.contribute: Count one of your deals: Plan and actuals
modelValidation.unreachable: The validation report can't be read just now. Try again in a minute.
modelValidation.noReport: The first report is written by the nightly validation task. Until then there is nothing to show.
modelValidation.libraryOff: The reference library is switched off
modelValidation.fitUntilSub: Default-risk outcomes after this year are newer data
modelValidation.claim_default: Predicted: S&P's cumulative default rate for the coverage-implied rating, over five years from closing. Observed: distress within those years.
modelValidation.claim_irr_range: Predicted: the plan's simulated IRR paths. Observed: how often the actual IRR fell inside their central 50%, 80% and 90%.
modelValidation.claim_loss: Predicted: the plan's share of simulated paths below 1x. Observed: deals that returned less than their equity.
modelValidation.notEnoughOverall: Not enough data: {n, plural, one {# case} other {# cases}}, statistics need {count}.
modelValidation.overallRange: {n, plural, one {# case} other {# cases}}: {levels}. Bias {bias} points. {verdict}
modelValidation.overallProbability: {n, plural, one {# case} other {# cases}}: predicted {predicted}, observed {observed}, bias {bias} points. {verdict}
modelValidation.hiddenNote: Too few users' deals to show
modelValidation.consentNote: Lets this deal's plan-vs-actual result count in the model validation report: only counts and rates by region, sector, size and era, never the deal, its name or its figures. Switch off at any time; the next report leaves it out.
modelValidation.consentFailed: The choice couldn't be saved. Try again.

dealRisk.unit: Against companies and deals like it
dealRisk.comparing: Comparing the deal with companies like it…
dealRisk.noCountry: Choose the deal's country under Starting point to compare it with companies in its region.
dealRisk.noPeers: Fewer than {min} {industry} companies in {areas}, so the deal is not compared. Other regions' companies are not used.
dealRisk.scoreTested: How far leverage and price sit above the industry's, in spreads between industries. Tested on {cases, plural, one {# buyout} other {# buyouts}} in {region}: it ranked the distressed ones higher than leverage alone did ({model} against {baseline}).
dealRisk.scoreTooFew: Tested on {cases, plural, =0 {no buyouts} one {# buyout} other {# buyouts}} in {region}, too few to show a score. The comparison is shown.
dealRisk.scoreNotBetter: Not shown: in {region} it does not rank distressed buyouts better than leverage alone.
dealRisk.sourceNote: Listed companies' averages from {publisher}, {date}; not split by size.
dealRisk.dealsNoSector: Choose the deal's industry under Starting point to list reference deals like it.

distress.unitDeal: Rating band each year and the chance of default
distress.unitSimulated: Rating bands across the simulated paths
distress.businessRiskNote: S&P's business risk profile. With leverage it sets each year's rating band on Distress by year (Corporate Methodology, Table 3). Your choice, not a sourced figure.
distress.rowProbability: Chance of default in the year
distress.rowCumulative: Chance of default by year end
distress.rowMeanProbability: Mean chance of default in the year
distress.rowMeanCumulative: Mean chance of default by year end
distress.shown: Tested on {cases, plural, one {# buyout} other {# buyouts}} in {region}: it ranked the distressed ones higher than the year-one default risk did ({model} against {baseline}).
distress.notBetter: Chances of default are not shown: tested on {cases, plural, one {# buyout} other {# buyouts}} in {region}, they ranked the distressed ones no better than the year-one default risk ({model} against {baseline}). The bands are shown.
distress.tooFew: Chances of default are not shown: tested on {cases, plural, =0 {no buyouts} one {# buyout} other {# buyouts}} in {region}, too few. The bands are shown.
distress.reads: Each year's band is the weaker of EBIT / interest (Damodaran's coverage table) and debt at the start of the year over the year's EBITDA at business risk {business} (S&P Tables 17 and 3). Chances of default: S&P's cumulative default rates, {table}.
